# Badriyah Alsalem (بدرية السالم)

> Badriyah Alsalem is an architect and researcher interested in the environment, astronomy, history, and spatial philosophy. She is inspired by deserts and their systems of navigation and timekeeping, and by how language and folklore preserve environmental knowledge.

Also written: بدريه السالم, Badriyah AlSalem, Badriyah Al-Salem.

## About

- Bachelor of Architecture, Kuwait University (2023).
- Master of Science in Computational Design Practices, Columbia University Graduate School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation (GSAPP), New York (2025). Her thesis, Resistant Atlas: Names of the Sun, received the Most Outstanding Capstone Award.
- Her thesis has grown into an ongoing research practice that brings together essays, instruments, digital tools, and spatial installations.
- Her professional path moves between architecture, research, academia, and creative direction. She works as an architect in Kuwait, designing hotels, and leads her independent practice, RUMMA Studio.
- She previously worked in AlUla as an amateur astronomy researcher and guide, leading stargazing experiences and lectures, researching Arabic astronomical folklore, and developing star maps, public programs, and astronomy workshops.
- She is an artist-in-residence at Diriyah Art Futures in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and a participant in the Sharjah Architecture Triennial 2026.

## Websites

- [Resistant Atlas](https://resistantatlas.com/): her research. An ongoing research and design project that studies how pre-modern Arab knowledge systems translated the environment into language, orientation, and time.
- [RUMMA Studio](https://rummastudio.com/): her design practice, working in architecture and cultural astronomy.
